wu: Warm-up: 'Plan Relay' - students stand in teams, take turns running to the board to write one weekend plan using 'going to' (e.g., 'I'm going to visit my grandmother'), then high-five the next teammate. Fastest team with 5 correct sentences wins.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Plan Pictionary' - draw a future action (e.g., 'studying') for teammates to guess and say with 'going to'
Alternative 2: 'Quick Poll' - raise hands for 'going to the beach' vs 'going to the mountains', then say why
pres: Presentation: Show a flashcard of a boy with a backpack and plane. Model: 'He's going to travel to Spain because he wants to see his cousin. He's going to leave on Friday after school.' Elicit similar plans with 'because' and time clauses. Check by asking 'Why is he going?' and 'When is he leaving?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short story about a girl's Eid plans with 'after' and 'before' clauses
Alternative 2: Roleplay a teacher-student dialogue about Green March plans with 'going to' + reasons
prac: Guided practice: 'Plan Sort' - students get cards with time clauses (e.g., 'After lunch') and actions (e.g., 'I'm going to call my friend'). They match and make full sentences. Monitor for correct use of 'going to' and connectors.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Sentence Race' - teams race to unscramble sentences like 'I / going to / study / before the exam'
Alternative 2: 'Plan Chains' - each student adds one 'going to' sentence to a partner's plan
ls: Listening slot: Play a dialogue about two friends comparing Eid holiday plans. Students listen and fill in a chart with 'What' and 'Why' for each person. Play twice, then check in pairs.
re: Reactivation game: 'Freeze Plans' - students walk around saying their plans (e.g., 'I'm going to bake a cake'). When teacher shouts 'Freeze!', they stop and say what they'll do 'after' (e.g., 'After baking, I'm going to share it').
prod: Production task: 'Plan Complication Roleplay' - pairs receive cards with a plan (e.g., 'going to a concert') and a problem (e.g., 'your ticket is lost'). They roleplay discussing solutions using 'going to' + 'if' (e.g., 'If I can't find it, I'm going to buy a new one').
rw: Reading and writing slot: Read a short email about a Labour Day trip to the Rif Mountains. Students underline 'before/after' clauses. Then write a 60-word reply using 3 'going to' sentences with time clauses.
st: Story + goodbye: Read a short story about a teen's Independence Day plans with 'going to' and connectors. End with: 'Today we learned to talk about plans with reasons and time clauses. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams race to write 'going to' sentences on the board
Match time clauses with actions to make full sentences
Stop and say what you'll do 'after' your plan
Solve problems in future plans using 'going to'
Draw future actions for teammates to guess
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 3-step plan for their next holiday with 'before/after' clauses
Support: Use a sentence frame: 'I'm going to ___ because ___ after ___'
hw: Homework 1: Read a text about a Green March celebration and answer 3 questions in full sentences using 'going to'
Homework 2: Write a 60-word email to a friend about your weekend plans with 2 'because' and 1 'after' clause
Homework 3: Record a 1-minute voice note describing your next holiday plan using 'going to'
tip: Use local holidays (Eid, Green March) to make plans relatable. Teens engage more when future plans connect to their cultural experiences.
